name: HISv3
goal: Automated regression coverage for HISv3, the hospital information system, from the product map down to every test case

brd.problem: HISv3 has 444 features across four parts and about 1,700 catalogued test cases, but only about a third are automated. Regressions in registration, billing, clinical forms and the vendor and corporate integrations are found by hand, late, and without a record of what was checked.
goals: Every PROD and DEV-DONE feature is traceable to a user story, a scenario and an automated test, so a release candidate carries a coverage number rather than an opinion.
All P0 and P1 cases run unattended against staging and report pass or fail per case.
A case that cannot be automated says why, in the catalog, with an owner and a reason category.
The test scripts and the plan stay in step: what GAOS plans and what the QA tools run are the same list of cases.
scope: The HISv3 product map: Part A core HIS, Part B omnichannel and vendor integration, Part C the Primaya mobile app API, Part D corporate and web platform.
REST, GraphQL, SSE and WebSocket API tests, RabbitMQ consumer tests and web end-to-end tests against the real backend on staging or local.
The test catalog: epics, user stories, positive and negative cases, priority, level and status.
A two-way sync between GAOS (the plan) and the QA tools (the scripts and their results).
outOfScope: Production. No test targets a production host and none is ever added.
Unit tests of the product repositories; they live with the product code.
Native mobile device runs, which need an emulator and have their own toolchain.
rules: Every test case has a stable id (TC-<EPIC>-NNN), is never reused, and carries a polarity, a level, a priority and a status.
A case is covered only when it is automated, its spec exists and it passes; a case that is blocked, manual-only or wont must carry a reason of the form category:detail.
Every behaviour has a positive and a negative case; negative cases cover missing auth, wrong role, invalid input, not found and the business rules.
Tests are independent and own their data: unique e2e-prefixed values, cleanup registered at creation, no dependence on pre-existing counts.
No secrets, real patient data or production URLs in the repository, logs, fixtures or test titles.
A failing test is never weakened to pass: the cause is found, or the case is recorded as a defect with a ticket.
GAOS owns the plan (what a case is, what is decided about it); the QA tools own the facts of execution (is there a script, did the last run pass). Neither writes the other's fields.
metrics: Automated share of non-wont cases, overall and per epic (today about 29 percent).
Automated share of P0 and P1 cases.
Share of PROD features with at least one automated case.
Pass rate of the last full staging run, and the count of epics with a failing case.

decisions.title: Playwright with TypeScript, API-level and end-to-end tests only; unit tests stay in the product repositories
The catalog's case id is the join key between the plan and the scripts, and an id is never reused
One writer per field: GAOS writes planning fields, the QA tools write automation facts, and the newest run wins

policies.title: Stack and layout of the HISv3 test repository
policies.body:
- Tests are Playwright with TypeScript, Node 22.19 or newer. npm and Bun are both supported; no script hard-codes bun.
- Folders mirror the product repositories: src/<layer>/<service or app>/ pairs with tests/<layer>/<service or app>/.
- Specs reach the system only through API clients under src/api and page objects under src/web. No raw requests or raw selectors in a spec.
- Targets are TEST_ENV=local and staging. Production hosts are blocked in config/env.ts and that guard is never weakened.
- There is no mock server: tests run against a real local service or staging.
- Which HISv3 services are in scope, and which are active, is docs/hisv3-services.md.

policies.title: How a test is written
policies.body:
- Import test and expect only from @fixtures. TypeScript strict, no any, no ts-ignore, every promise awaited.
- One behaviour per test; the title states the expected behaviour in the present tense. No conditionals inside a test.
- Never sleep or wait for network idle. Use web-first assertions or expect.poll.
- Locators in this order: role, label, placeholder, text, test id. No XPath, no long CSS chains.
- REST: assert status and contract, and cover happy path, 401, 403, 400, 404 and the business-rule codes. GraphQL: assert the error code and path, not only the HTTP status.
- Build payloads with factories; unique values start with e2e-. Register cleanup immediately after creating data.
- Never add a dependency without approval, and update both lockfiles when one is approved.

policies.title: Secrets, patient data and environments
policies.body:
- No credentials, tokens, cookies, phone numbers, national ids or real patient data anywhere: code, fixtures, snapshots, logs, commit messages or test titles.
- Only *.example env files are committed. Real values come from the shell or the password manager.
- On shared environments a test may modify only data it created. Anything else is destructive and must be guarded.
- Do not paste the contents of env files, .auth or test-data/private into prompts, pull requests or issues.
- Never add a production URL.

policies.title: The test catalog and the definition of done
policies.body:
- The checklist of what to test is docs/test-catalog/: epic, story, then positive and negative cases with a status of planned, automated, blocked, manual-only or wont.
- A case that is blocked, manual-only or wont needs a reason of the form category:detail, with category one of defect, not-needed, blocked, unsafe, manual-only, deferred, other. A defect reason names the defect id.
- Never delete or weaken a case to avoid writing a reason; set the status and the reason and let the reviewer decide.
- Every new or changed test maps to a TC row: update its status and spec path in the same change and run the catalog check.
- Priorities: P0 is smoke, P1 is regression, P2 normal, P3 edge. Automate P0 and P1 first, and the DEV-DONE and PROD features of the product map first.
- Done means: the check passes, the new spec passes three times in a row, the catalog row is updated, the data is cleaned up and the summary states what was and was not run.

policies.title: The two-way sync between GAOS and the QA tools
policies.body:
- The case id (TC-<EPIC>-NNN) joins the plan and the scripts.
- GAOS owns the planning fields: epic, module, features, user story, scenario, polarity, level, priority, decision and reason. The QA tools own the automation facts: implemented, spec, result, run time and run reference.
- Report a result only for a case that exists in the catalog. An unknown case id is refused, never created from the QA side.
- A run record is the result together with the time it ran; an older run never overwrites a newer one.
- A script that exists for a case GAOS parked (blocked, manual-only or wont) is reported as needing a decision. Do not change the decision yourself.
- Batches hold at most 200 items.

The QA tools that will run the scripts and exchange results with GAOS.
